dimensions.name: Bank size & dedicated volume
dimensions.evidence: The bank has a substantial number of items (9451 active, 8487 served), with a significant portion enriched (53.7%).
dimensions.gap: While the volume is high, the quality and depth of items are inconsistent, as seen in the sample.

dimensions.name: NBME blueprint / systems coverage
dimensions.evidence: Coverage is uneven, with strong representation in internal medicine and emergency medicine but very thin in obstetrics, ethics, and infectious disease.
dimensions.gap: Key areas like ethics and infectious disease are underrepresented, which are crucial for Step 3.

dimensions.name: Item craft (stem/options/clinical reasoning)
dimensions.evidence: Many items lack well-crafted vignettes and balanced options, with frequent mismatches in item type and content.
dimensions.gap: Items often have weak distractors and lack complexity, reducing their effectiveness in testing clinical reasoning.

dimensions.name: Basic-science ↔ clinical integration (or next-step management for Step 2/3)
dimensions.evidence: Some items integrate clinical scenarios well, but many lack depth in decision-making frameworks typical of Step 3.
dimensions.gap: There is a need for better integration of clinical reasoning and decision-making processes.

dimensions.name: Biostats / ethics / CCS readiness (as applicable)
dimensions.evidence: Biostats and ethics are poorly represented, with mismatches in item types and weak vignette integration.
dimensions.gap: Critical areas for Step 3, such as biostats and ethics, are inadequately covered.

dimensions.name: Rationale / teachability (UWorld-depth proxy)
dimensions.evidence: Explanations are often overly detailed or lack depth, with insufficient discussion of incorrect options.
dimensions.gap: Explanations need to be more concise and educational, focusing on key decision points and alternative options.

dimensions.name: High-yield disease & pharm readiness
dimensions.evidence: Common high-yield topics are covered, but the depth and quality of items vary significantly.
dimensions.gap: While coverage is broad, the depth and challenge level of items need improvement.

dimensions.name: Quality gates & consistency
dimensions.evidence: Inconsistencies in item categorization and quality, with frequent critical flags in sample items.
dimensions.gap: Quality control measures need strengthening to ensure consistency and alignment with USMLE standards.

bank.examTakerVerdict: The QBank provides a broad range of questions but lacks the depth and consistency needed for high-level USMLE Step 3 preparation. It may serve as a supplementary resource but should not be relied upon as the primary study tool.
topStrengths: Strong representation in internal medicine and emergency medicine.
topGaps: Inadequate coverage of ethics and biostats.
Weak integration of clinical reasoning and decision-making.
prioritizedActions: Enhance coverage and depth in underrepresented areas like ethics and biostats.
Improve item crafting to include well-balanced options and realistic vignettes.
Strengthen explanations to focus on key decision points and alternative options.
Implement stricter quality control measures to ensure consistency and alignment with USMLE standards.
